articles.title: Navigating shoot apical meristem plasticity for plant adaptation
articles.desc: Plants exhibit striking developmental plasticity, driven by stem cell populations within meristematic tissues such as the shoot apical meristem (SAM). While the genetic networks governing stem cell homeostasis are well-characterized, recent studies reveal that the SAM also functions as an active environmental sensor to modulate growth plasticity. This Tansley review synthesizes advances in how the SAM perceives and integrates key environmental signals - including light, temperature, oxygen, and humidity - to direct adaptive growth. We detail the molecular mechanisms, such as photoreceptor-mediated activation, thermal resilience pathways, hypoxia sensing, hydraulic dynamics, and mechanical signalling, that regulate stem cell activity. Furthermore, we explore how these environmental cues couple with developmental programs to fine-tune meristem function and organogenesis. By drawing parallels to the environmental regulation of root meristem development, we highlight conserved sensing and signalling modules within meristematic tissues that influence plant growth plasticity. Examining this interplay both in shoot and in root meristems, from evolutionary and applied perspectives, underscores how environmental responsiveness of stem cell niches regulates plant adaptation, informing strategies for engineering climate-resilient crops.

articles.desc: The scale of amphibian and reptile translocations over the past 16 years necessitates a reassessment of current practices since the last major review in 2009. We conducted a literature review of translocations from 2007 to 2023 and identified 313 case studies encompassing conservation-, mitigation-, and research-related translocations. This spread is a concern, especially for novel and emerging potentially catastrophic fungal diseases such as ophidiomycosis (snake fungal disease). Our results reveal biases from omitting country-specific financing conditions and highlight the need for climate finance across many sectors.

articles.desc: Context Habitat loss and fragmentation are among the most significant drivers of biodiversity decline worldwide. articles.desc: Supply–demand imbalance of ecosystem services (ES) is a core challenge under rapid urbanization. This study quantified how policy-oriented land-use pathways reshape ES supply–demand relationships across the urban–rural gradient, and located the spatial shift of their equilibrium point. articles.title: Context-dependent effects of land-sparing and land-sharing strategies on urban bird diversity
articles.desc: Urban green spaces play a vital role in sustaining biodiversity, particularly bird communities, in rapidly urbanizing regions. articles.desc: Ongoing climate change has intensified compound climate extremes, increasing the long-term exposure of ecosystems to compound climatic stress and posing growing risks to ecosystem services (ESs) through complex and spatially heterogeneous associations. articles.desc: Context Land-system change reshapes landscapes, but its ecological consequences depend on land-use type, management, and disturbance, not vegetation cover alone. articles.desc: Inconsistent findings regarding the impact of urban blue-green space patterns on regional thermal environments hinder the practical application of research in landscape ecology. articles.desc: Context Species distribution models combine environmental and occurrence data to map and predict habitat suitability for a species. articles.desc: Habitat loss is a major driver of biodiversity decline, particularly for wide-ranging carnivores that depend on connected landscapes. articles.desc: Elephants were a major driver of tree stem mortality in Africa, but their impacts are now spatially constrained and they no longer topple trees across the continent. articles.title: N-glycosylation code diversifies paralogous chitinases to balance plant immunity and growth
articles.desc: Nature Plants, Published online: 05 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41477-026-02420-7 This work reveals an N-glycosylation code that distinguishes two Arabidopsis chitinase paralogues, directing them to produce or degrade immunogenic chitin oligomers. This enables plants to gain chitin-triggered fungal resistance without a growth penalty.

articles.title: Maternal epigenetic regulation of embryonic patterning in plants
articles.desc: Nature Plants, Published online: 01 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41477-026-02421-6 Post-fertilization remodelling of H3K27me3 in integuments regulates the timely activation of auxin transport genes, thereby facilitating maternal-to-embryo auxin transport and shaping embryonic patterning.

articles.title: SNI1 governs how temperature reshapes crossovers and genetic diversity
articles.desc: Nature Plants, Published online: 23 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41477-026-02413-6 Cooler temperature alters the frequency and genomic sites of chromosomal DNA exchange during reproduction in Arabidopsis thaliana. This response depends on SNI1, a chromosome-architecture factor that acts as a temperature-sensitive brake on crossover formation and helps to determine the genetic combinations passed to the next generation.

articles.title: SNI1/NSE5 is a cold-sensitive brake on class II crossovers in Arabidopsis
articles.desc: Nature Plants, Published online: 23 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41477-026-02400-x Cold temperature alters meiotic recombination in Arabidopsis by weakening SNI1/NSE5, a chromosome architecture factor that normally limits class II crossovers and shapes where genetic exchange occurs.

articles.title: Long-term biomass growth unimpeded by short-term photosynthetic decoupling
articles.desc: Nature Plants, Published online: 22 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41477-026-02418-1 Using long-term observations and global vegetation models, Nguyen et al. show that the decoupling between photosynthesis and plant wood growth reported in recent studies neither implies sink limitation nor constrains long-term biomass growth.

articles.title: Engineering resilient forests
articles.desc: Nature Plants, Published online: 17 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41477-026-02414-5 Climate change leads to changes in precipitation distribution and the frequency of extreme weather conditions. For temperate forests to survive this may require a targeted forest engineering approach.
